minutes.headline: Committee picked a $12,000 search consultant paid from school choice and set a roughly 3% FY19 school budget
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a parent's complaint about the March 14 student walkout and a promise to draft a walkout policy. The committee heard an athletic advisory fundraising proposal, chose a superintendent search consultant, and took up central office contracts. The superintendent also described the FY19 budget bottom line to bring to the Finance Committee.

Resident asked about the executive session and said the contract is not on the website.

what_happened.line: The committee accepted a bid from MASC for the superintendent search consultant, paid from the school choice account; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The committee approved the central office personnel contracts for fiscal years 2019 through 2021; the vote was not audible in the captions.
The committee allowed the superintendent to bring a school budget bottom line, reflecting roughly a 3 percent increase, to the Finance Committee.
The consultant's first meeting was set for Monday, March 26.
A parent asked for a policy on student walkouts; a subgroup will meet again and put the item on the next agenda.

why_it_matters: The FY19 school budget bottom line is the starting point for the school share of the town budget, mostly taxes, that residents will be asked to vote on.
The search consultant is paid from school choice funds, not the general school budget, and the central office contracts set salary costs for three fiscal years.
